name: Rice University
character: The heavily wooded campus is organized into quadrangles with over 4,000 trees and shrubs and features uniform Byzantine-style buildings made of sand and pink-colored bricks with large archways and columns.

landmarks.name: Lovett Hall
landmarks.quote: Lovett Hall, named for Rice's first president, is the university's landmark building. Through its Sallyport arch
landmarks.look: Asymmetrical Byzantine-style brick building with a Sallyport arch and columns.

landmarks.name: Academic Quad
landmarks.quote: The Academic Quad, anchored by a statue of founder William Marsh Rice, includes Ralph Adams Cram's masterpiece, the asymmetrical Lovett Hall
landmarks.look: Central open quadrangle anchored by a seated bronze statue facing Lovett Hall.

landmarks.name: First Community Stadium
landmarks.quote: The on-campus football facility, First Community Stadium, opened in 1950 with a capacity of 70,000 seats.
landmarks.look: Large 47,000-seat football stadium on the western end of campus.

landmarks.name: Fondren Library
landmarks.quote: the asymmetrical Lovett Hall, the original administrative building; Fondren Library;
landmarks.look: Plain library building on the Academic Quad.

landmarks.name: Lynn R. Lowrey Arboretum
landmarks.quote: The Lynn R. Lowrey Arboretum, consisting of more than 4000 trees and shrubs is spread throughout the campus.
landmarks.look: Wooded grounds with over 4,000 trees and shrubs spread across campus.

landmarks.name: Engineering Quad
landmarks.quote: In the Engineering Quad, a trinity of sculptures by Michael Heizer, collectively entitled 45 Degrees, 90 Degrees, 180 Degrees, are flanked by Abercrombie Laboratory
landmarks.look: Quadrangle featuring three geometric sculptures flanked by engineering buildings.

landmarks.name: Duncan Hall
landmarks.quote: Duncan Hall, Rice's computational engineering building, was designed to encourage collaboration between the four different departments situated there.
landmarks.look: Computational engineering hall with a foyer inspired by many world cultures.

landmarks.name: Herzstein Hall
landmarks.quote: Herzstein Hall, the original physics building and home to the largest amphitheater on campus
landmarks.look: Plain academic hall housing the largest amphitheater on campus.
